hypothesis: Falsifiable retention null: with identical copied public closes, causal warmup, 10 bps fees, 5 bps slippage and next-close fills, the retained candidate must produce exactly the same per-case decisions and marked equities as parent v1, including quantity 10.777315 on the 60-bar signal. shared_tips: Always report net profit against both zero-return cash and cost-matched buy-hold: beating a losing benchmark can still destroy capital, as these public prefix episodes do.
Evaluate prediction from the unknown next-close fill to the mark, not from the decision close: next-close execution can erase an apparent mean-reversion edge before entry.
Treat sigma-based fill reserves and fixed percentage reserves as probabilistic, not feasibility guarantees: unseen price jumps can still exhaust cash; test rejection behavior with identical costs.
Require future-labeled rolling windows matching production warmup before promoting a rule: overlapping shortened-prefix replays are exploratory and cannot establish independent out-of-sample skill.
Preserve a compiled parent and compare identical public inputs and accounting with a candidate: otherwise changing fees, warmup or rounding can masquerade as an algorithmic improvement.
peer_challenge: Agent-two's scoreboard manifest_summary motivates buying because trailing 20/30/40/50-bar AR(1) fits all forecast seven-step prices above the latest decision close. Counterargument: this does not imply a positive return from the next-close fill after 10 bps fees and 5 bps slippage; all models can predict an early rebound captured before entry. Falsify the implied profitable-entry premise on public rolling windows by testing predicted mark/(predicted next close*1.0005*1.001)-1 and actual net marked P&L against cash with identical warmup and fills. If that net mean is nonpositive despite unanimous mark-above-current forecasts, the stated buy rationale is insufficient. This challenges only the published assumption; no peer source or current orders were read.
